Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers survived the late rally of the Carolina Panthers to notch a 27-19 victory at Lambeau Field on Thursday. The defense played a huge part in crunch time, including sacking Bryce Young in the last 20 seconds to seal the hard-earned win. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “LaFleur uses the word ‘savant’ about Jonathan Gannon,” wrote Huber on X. Gannon is in his first year in Green Bay, energizing the defense with his tactical flexibility and ability to maximize talent. Like LaFleur, Evan Williams gushed about Gannon, stressing that it is a “big trust thing.” “JG feels confident in each of us, which is big. item.title: How talking about Man Utd's cycle of doom became an industry
item.description: Gary Neville and Michael Carrick were Manchester United and England team-mates [Getty Images] Manchester United. More a high-volume content farm than a football club these days. Michael Carrick's starring role in what has become one of the nation's favourite soap operas has been extended for at least another week, with the 45-year-old set to be in charge for Saturday's visit to Chelsea. Good news - you'd think - for Carrick. But even better news for Amazon's All or Nothing camera crews, who have been given "unprecedented" access to document the behind-the-scenes goings-on at Old Trafford this season. United fans will presumably be relieved when the football resumes on Saturday, if only to break up the constant stream of opinion for 90 minutes. But while the wall-to-wall reporting of one of the world's biggest football clubs is hardly new, the unrelenting coverage from former players is a growing phenomenon. It is easier to name the Manchester United legends who don't have a platform from which they scrutinise the club's every move than those that do - and it begs the question whether the club's demise has been industrialised into a content-creating machine. 'It doesn't really help in any way' Whether supporters feel comments from ex-players are damaging or not differs from fan to fan, but what cannot be denied is how difficult it is to escape their views. Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville provided scathing on-air commentary during United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last Sunday, before conducting a post-match podcast in the Old Trafford gantry in which he accused some of their players of being unprofessional. "There's a couple of them... I live in Manchester and they're not that professional, some of them," Neville stated. "I've got no time for them. There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time. Don't eat the right things. Don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every single day." But it's digital and streaming platforms that are re-defining a new age of analysis. Neville launched The Overlap in 2021, and its success across video and podcast platforms has seen the channel become one of the most influential outlets in sports media. On Tuesday, Wayne Rooney appeared on Neville's Manchester United-dedicated YouTube channel 'Stick to United' where he said Carrick's players "need a firework up their a***". Neville has since hosted his own The Overlap show where he said managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good", while ex-United captain Roy Keane said Carrick and his backroom staff are "lucky boys" to still be in jobs. Neville acquired a network of YouTube channels from United influencer Mark Goldbridge last summer, which has significantly increased the channel's coverage of the club. item.title: Ciao, San Siro! AC Milan and Inter announce record-breaking €650m naming rights deal for new Generali Stadium
item.description: AC Milan v FC Internazionale: Semi Final - Coppa Italia - Getty Images Sport The iconic skyline of Milan is set for a historic transformation as the city's two footballing heavyweights prepare to move into a state-of-the-art new home. In a move that signals a massive shift in the financial landscape of Serie A, AC Milan and Inter have officially secured a record-breaking naming rights partnership with Italian insurance giant Generali for their future shared arena. Record-breaking deal for a new era Milan and Inter have agreed a staggering 20-year naming rights contract with Generali, which ESPN reports is worth €650 million (£545m/$725m). The new 71,500-capacity venue will be officially known as the Generali Stadium, effectively replacing the historic San Siro. The clubs purchased the required land from the city last November for €197m , paving the way for the eventual demolition of their legendary current home. Construction is targeted to begin in 2028, with the first matches scheduled for the 2031-32 campaign, pending necessary approvals. Spearheaded by respective ownership groups RedBird Capital Partners and Oaktree, the stadium project also anchors a wider urban regeneration plan featuring new retail, leisure, and green spaces. The massive financial commitment eclipses the $700m agreement struck by Crypto.com in 2021 for the Los Angeles arena shared by the Lakers and Kings. It stands as a monumental boost for the two Serie A giants as they look to modernise and bridge the matchday revenue gap with Europe's elite. A new symbol for Milano. A new home for future generations of fans. Generali Stadium 🏟️ @GENERALI pic.twitter.com/c7D0827E7T — AC Milan (@acmilan) October 29, 2026 Ispirato all'eredità architettonica di Milano e progettato per il futuro. Un nuovo stadio che unisce design, innovazione e sostenibilità in una delle opere più ambiziose mai immaginate per la città. pic.twitter.com/YiQLWaShqO — Inter ⭐⭐ (@Inter) October 29, 2026 Inspired by Milanese heritage In a joint news release, the clubs proudly described the Generali partnership as "one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport." The statement accompanied the unveiling of the stadium's official renderings, which showcase a striking architectural vision for the city. The design, a collaboration between Foster+Partners and MANICA, draws direct inspiration from "the intricate craftsmanship of the Duomo di Milano." Lord Norman Foster and David Manica, who previously teamed up to design London's Wembley Stadium, have conceptualised a continuous 360-degree bowl split across two tiers. Special attention has been given to the fan experience. The iconic 'Curvas' will feature single, steep walls with seating inclinations of up to 37 degrees to maximise atmosphere and visual impact. item.title: Hyrox athlete who soiled herself in race tells BBC she put others at risk but says backlash was traumatic
item.description: Watch: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk tells BBC An Australian athlete has admitted putting others at risk by continuing to race after soiling herself during an endurance sports event. Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that." Challenged over why she carried on, she said: "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect." The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was "traumatic". She also said she had considered walking away from the sport, in which she holds a world record. Hyrox sees participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing, and lunges while carrying a sandbag. The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, in northern Germany, and is now held across the world. Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning [Getty Images] Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea. Images of faecal matter on parts of her body were then shared widely online. Asked whether officials should have stopped her, she said no-one encouraged her to do so at the time. Hyrox's co-founder, Moritz Fürste, has issued an apology saying it had been a mistake not to react immediately during the race. New rules have now been introduced giving race directors the power to remove athletes if their vomit, urine or faeces pose a risk of contamination or threaten the welfare of themselves or others in a race that is primarily held indoors using shared equipment. Although initially defiant in a now-deleted Instagram post, Wietrzyk apologised in the week after the Beijing event and said she would forfeit the win and retroactively withdraw from the race. Due to compete in Hamburg on Friday, she said she was "nervous" about her return and hoped that the high-profile incident would not define her. "I don't want it to become my identity," she said. Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win clouded her judgement [BBC] In her first interview since Beijing, Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning but had gone into the race "feeling fresh, feeling really, really good". "It was a very sudden experience," she told the BBC. "It wasn't until about halfway through the race where everything did transpire... item.title: Azmatullah Omarzai scripts history after walking in at 5/4, smashes T20I world record
item.description: Azmatullah Omarzai produced a stunning rescue act with the bat, smashing a record-breaking century to help Afghanistan recover from a disastrous start and post 221/7 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Thursday. Walking in with Afghanistan reeling at 5/4, Omarzai launched a counter-attack that completely changed the course of the innings. He hammered 116 off just 50 balls, striking five fours and 12 sixes at an astonishing strike rate of 232. With the effort, Omarzai registered the highest individual score by a batter coming in at No. 6 or lower in T20Is involving Full Member nations. He went past the previous record of 89, scored by former Afghanistan captain Mohammad Nabi against Ireland in 2017. The record-breaking knock also put Omarzai ahead of Sam Billings (87 against West Indies in 2019), Cameron White (85 not out against Sri Lanka in 2010) and David Miller (85 not out against Pakistan in 2021) on the list. Afghanistan's innings had been in complete disarray after Zimbabwe's bowlers reduced them to 5/4. Several top-order batters departed cheaply, while Sediqullah Atal managed just 17 off 21 deliveries before falling in the ninth over. Omarzai found an ideal partner in Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai, and the duo launched a remarkable recovery. They added 142 runs off only 59 balls for the sixth wicket, with Ijaz contributing a blistering 52 off 27 deliveries, including five fours and three sixes. The partnership was finally broken when Ijaz fell with the score at 180. Omarzai continued his assault before being dismissed in the 19th over, having already produced one of the finest rescue acts in Afghanistan's T20I history. Captain Rashid Khan provided a spectacular finish, smashing an unbeaten 25 off just six balls, including four sixes. Mujeeb Ur Rahman remained not out on two as Afghanistan closed their innings at 221/7, scoring at 11.05 runs per over. Rashid also achieved a major milestone during the match, becoming the first bowler to claim 200 wickets in T20Is. Zimbabwe fall short despite Sikandar Raza's century Zimbabwe were unable to overcome the imposing target despite a determined effort from captain Sikandar Raza, who scored his second T20I century. Raza fought till the end, but the visitors ultimately fell short, with Afghanistan's early batting collapse proving to be a distant memory after Omarzai's extraordinary intervention. Tafadzwa Tsiga offered valuable support on his debut, while the dismissal of Ryan Burl dealt another blow to Zimbabwe's hopes. The victory also extended Afghanistan's remarkable dominance in the rivalry, marking their eighth consecutive T20I series win against Zimbabwe. The visitors are yet to win a T20I series against Afghanistan.

item.title: Kings' overtime coaching overhaul leads to dramatic win over Senators
item.description: Los Angeles Kings players celebrate a goal during a game against the Ottawa Senators on October 29, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. The Los Angeles Kings found a way to win a game they shouldn’t have needed to find a way to win on Thursday night. They might have a change in coaching strategy to thank for that. After blowing a 5-1 third-period lead, the Kings defeated the Ottawa Senators 6-5 in overtime behind Quinton Byfield’s game-winner. But almost as interesting as the wild swings of the game was something Drew Doughty revealed after it ended. “It’s the first year in my whole career that we’ve ever actually worked on three-on-three,” the Kings’ captain said. “A lot of credit to the coaches in that area. We worked on it in camp. We worked on it before the season started, and they had a bit of a game plan, which we didn’t really have before either. So a lot of credit to them for making us work on it.” If the Kings ever had an offseason where they needed to improve that aspect of their game, it was this past one. They lost an NHL-record 20 overtime and shootout games in 2025-26, a huge part of the reason they finished with the Western Conference’s second wild-card spot and were swept out of the playoffs in the first round. First-year head coach Peter Laviolette came in and wanted to make sure the Kings didn’t post those numbers again. “There’s definitely a method to the madness, and there’s got to be a buy-in to that, and I think the players bought in,” Laviolette said. “There’s a lot of review that went through it, and there’s things that we talk about prior to games and then after games — the overtime games — and reviewing that. And I think the players have done a really good job of executing them.” Byfield, who scored with a burst of energy straight off the bench, went into more detail about what specifically the Kings focused on in their three-on-three practices. “Just trying to handle the puck as much as we can,” he said. “Obviously taking the right shots. item.description: Arsenal FC v Everton - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal are preparing to launch negotiations over an extended deal for first-choice goalkeeper David Raya despite the Spaniard recently admitting he would like to play in his homeland one day. Meanwhile, neither Barcelona nor Real Madrid are expected to make an imminent move for the 31-year-old shot-stopper in upcoming transfer windows. Gunners plan fresh contract talks According to Football Insider , the north London hierarchy want to tie their Spanish custodian down beyond his current 2028 expiration date to fend off any future interest from La Liga. Speculation linking him with Spain's two biggest clubs emerged after he told Spanish media last week that he hopes to play in his native top flight eventually . However, the goalkeeper insisted in the same interview that he remains content at the Emirates Stadium. Spanish giants lack goalkeeping vacancy Having silenced initial sceptics following his move from Brentford to establish himself as the Premier League's standout goalkeeper in recent seasons, Raya registered his fifth clean sheet in eight top-flight outings against Everton last weekend before narrowly losing out on Monday's Yashin Trophy to international team-mate Unai Simon . Explaining why a switch to Spain is unlikely soon on the Transfer Insider podcast, journalist Pete O'Rourke said: "If he were to leave Arsenal, there's no immediate opening for one of the big boys in Spain right now as well. Barcelona have got Joan Garcia, and it looks like Courtois is going to sign a new contract at Real Madrid as well, so I don't see any opening for David Raya right now. "The player is happy at Arsenal, and obviously Arsenal are very happy with him, so I think any potential move back to his native Spain will be probably on the back burner for a while just yet." Arteta jokes about Spanish return Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta has extracted the best form of Raya's career in north London and has no intention of letting his compatriot depart in the near future . Asked last weekend about his number one's desire to play in their homeland one day, Arteta delivered a lighthearted response: "I think David has to play in Spain at some point...on the beach with his friends in the summer. For the next few years, he needs to play here for Arsenal." Contract extension tops club agenda With both Spanish heavyweights settled between the posts and Arteta determined to retain his star shot-stopper, formal discussions over a renewal past 2028 are expected to get underway shortly. Securing Raya's long-term future will allow the goalkeeper to focus fully on maintaining his impressive defensive record across the autumn schedule. Any potential dream move to La Liga will therefore remain on hold for the foreseeable future.

item.title: DeMarcus Cousins suggests a 'straight-up trade' for Timberwolves after Anthony Edwards' injury
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Anthony Edwards is expected to be out for around two months, and that is a huge blow for the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Ant-Man had a phenomenal start to the new NBA season, and he formed an instant connection with LaMelo Ball. The duo looked incredible together. However, Edwards has undergone surgery and will be on the sidelines for a while. The Timberwolves need a solution in his absence, and DeMarcus Cousins has shared an interesting suggestion. DeMarcus Cousins suggests Rudy Gobert for Anthony Davis trade Anthony Davis only joined the Washington Wizards in February this year and made his regular-season debut in the opening game of this season. The former Mavs star has missed several games due to injury in recent years, but on his day, he is up there with the best forwards in the NBA. That is perhaps why Cousins feels the Timberwolves and Wizards should explore a ‘straight-up trade’ that would see Davis and Rudy Gobert switch sides. The former NBA star thinks this move would benefit both parties, as Minnesota would get a replacement for Edwards while the Wizards will have a defensive anchor that they need. Cousins said on Gil’s Arena : “If the Wizards are feeling like it’s not a good move, with everything that’s going on in Minnesota right now with Ant and how much time he’s gonna miss, I say they do a straight-up trade for Rudy and AD. “Man, Rudy’s looking crazy. He’s shooting like 23 per cent at the rim or something like that. If they don’t want to extend AD, they might as well (get him). “I think it would be better for Minnesota all-around. They kind of get the other go-to guy, while Anthony is out, to go along with LaMelo. I think it works for both teams. The Wizards get their defensive anchor. I just thought about it.” Edwards’ absence certainly weakens the Timberwolves, and someone like Davis could guarantee them 20 points a night if they can get him and keep him fit. However, whether the Wizards will accept Gobert after his underwhelming recent performances is anyone’s guess. item.title: Kevin Durant Reacts to Jalen Williams & Cason Wallace Injuries
item.description: Kevin Durant Jalen Williams Cason Wallace Getty Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant reacted to the injuries suffered by Oklahoma City Thunder teammates Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Both Williams and Wallace were injured last weekend in a game between the Thunder and the Los Angeles Clippers. Williams has a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle, and after undergoing successful surgery, will likely be out for the season. Wallace, meanwhile, is also likely out for the season with a torn labrum, a crushing blow to a Thunder team that is looking to win the NBA Championship for the second time in three years. Kevin Durant Reacts to Thunder Injuries Speaking to reporters, the former Thunder superstar Durant shared his sympathies for his former franchise seeing two of its most important players go down with devastating injuries. “I just feel for him. Honestly, this is a brotherhood. We compete at the highest level against each other and we keep that on the floor. But to see one of your brothers in this thing go down with such a gruesome injury, especially at this age and having an injury history last year, just thinking about him. Thinking about his teammates. That’s tough to see, man,” Durant said. “This is a brotherhood. We want everybody healthy. We want everybody on the court doing what they do. But he knows that he has so much support around him. He has so much support around the league. Can’t wait to see him get back. Cason Wallace, too. Get well to all those boys.” Kevin Durant Having Another Big Year for Houston Speaking of Durant, the long-time Thunder star is in his second year with the Rockets, and he’s having another fantastic season for Houston. Through the first five games of the 2026-27 NBA season, the Rockets are 5-0, and Durant has played well, averaging 22.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game for a Houston squad that looks like it might be a contender in the stacked Western Conference. The Thunder are still one of the best teams in the West, but with Williams and Wallace out, perhaps Oklahoma City’s losses could be Houston’s gain this season. item.description: Last season's fixtures between Sheffield United and Wrexham were the first league meetings between the sides since the 1982-83 campaign [Getty Images] Just two points separate Sheffield United and Wrexham as the pair lock horns in the Championship at Bramall Lane on Friday night (20:00 GMT). The match-up pits Chris Wilder against his former Southampton youth team-mate Phil Parkinson. And despite the new nature of the somewhat unconventional rivalry between the clubs, the various sub-plots once again make for an intriguing encounter. "It's a tasty game," said Wilder. "It's not historical over 15, 20 to 25 years, it's a recent one, but it's gathered pace along the way." Having not met in 19 years, the Blades narrowly overcame then National League side Wrexham in a fourth round FA Cup replay in 2023, just months before the Red Dragons gained the first of three successive promotions under Parkinson. The Welsh side held their Championship counterparts to a 3-3 draw before losing 3-1 in the replay. But it served as an early signal that Wrexham were determined to compete with the big guns in the near future. "We were talking at a function last night, someone asked me what game typified the Wrexham team and one of them was the home game [against Sheffield United] in the FA Cup," Parkinson said this week. "We lost two players through injury in the first 10 minutes, we were 1-0 down but the determination of the group in that game was incredible. "There was a big gulf between the two clubs at the time, they were top end Championship, one of the best teams. "I think if you can encapsulate everything you'd want in a performance, obviously we didn't get the win, but in terms of the spirit, belief and the hunger, that was all on display." "I watched both games back this week," said Parkinson. "The 5-3 was probably one of the best games in the Championship in the whole season for any team. It was a great game of football." Given the significant changes made to both squads during the summer, Wilder is not dwelling on his side's pair of losses to the north Wales outfit last term. item.title: Game over for Liverpool forward: Talks resume over transfer away
item.description: Game over for Liverpool forward: Talks resume over transfer away Liverpool made big improvements to their frontline over the summer. While the Reds had to contend with the loss of Mohamed Salah they moved decisively for Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz. With Alexander Isak recovering his form - and Hugo Ekitike in the hunt to return from injury - all of a sudden Andoni Iraola is looking at his options very favourably up top. There is Rio Ngumoha as well as Cody Gakpo to factor in - while Lewis Koumas has proven to be a useful addition to the first-team squad too. What that means is uncertainty over some players already on the books - not least Federico Chiesa . Federico Chiesa is wanted by Inter The Italian, 29, joined Liverpool back in 2024 on a £12.5m deal from Juventus. The Euro 2020 winner secured a contract until 2028 - but so far it’s been a miserable time on Merseyside for Chiesa. Although he can count himself a Premier League title winner things haven’t gone to plan for the former Fiorentina attacker. He has been injured or unavailable for a lot of his time at Anfield thus far - and has rarely pulled up any trees on the occasions he’s featured in the first team . It was speculated over the summer that he would be moving to Inter Milan - so long as the Nerazzurri got rid of Luis Henrique. Alas Cristian Chivu was unable to move on his Brazilian winger - meaning Chiesa stayed. Talks resume for Inter - Chiesa deal A report in Tutto Mercato Web however is now claiming that a January deal to take Chiesa to Inter is ON. Talks have been resumed in recent days between the parties - meaning Chiesa could soon be free to kickstart his career in Serie A. “In recent days, Inter have inquired about long-time favourite Federico Chiesa, who could leave Liverpool in January to return to Serie A and relaunch his career after a difficult period in England,” the report reads. Chiesa is reported to be making around £5m per annum at Liverpool - wage demands beyond the capabilities of most Italian sides. Factor in a transfer fee and very quickly the prospect of a deal disappears for the Italian champions. Nonetheless the report adds that Chivu’s side are plotting a LOAN for Chiesa - a deal which would have a favourable outcome for all parties involved. “A loan deal until June is a viable solution, satisfying the needs of both parties.” What becomes of Chiesa beyond summer remains to be seen - when he will have one year left on his deal.

item.title: Appeal rejected! Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman slapped with three-match ban after Carabao Cup red card drama
item.description: Fleetwood Town v Arsenal - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Arsenal have suffered a significant setback in their efforts to protect teenage sensation Max Dowman after an independent commission dismissed their appeal against his recent red card. The 16-year-old attacker was sent off during a frustrating Carabao Cup evening for the Gunners, and the club's attempt to overturn the decision has officially fallen flat. Dowman sees red in Carabao Cup exit The 16-year-old was given his marching orders in the 85th minute of Arsenal's Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town. The late dismissal followed a heavy challenge from Harrison Neal, with the teenager reacting poorly and kicking out at his opponent. Mikel Arteta's side ultimately exited the competition on penalties following a tense 1-1 draw. Hoping to spare their academy star a lengthy domestic suspension, the north London club formally challenged the referee's decision on grounds of wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment. FA confirms appeal dismissal Those hopes were quickly dashed when the Football Association shut down Arsenal's attempts to clear the youngster's name. Taking to X on Thursday , an FA spokesperson released a statement confirming that the original on-field decision would be upheld by an independent panel. "An independent Regulatory Commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Max Dowman," the governing body announced. The statement continued: "The Arsenal player was sent off during their EFL Cup game against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday 27 October and will be suspended for three matches." The FA also clarified that full written reasons for the commission's verdict will be published in due course. Arteta demands emotional control Addressing the media immediately after the midweek defeat, Arteta shed light on his tactical and mental expectations for the squad. While the Spanish manager admitted he had not yet spoken directly to Dowman regarding the dismissal, he hinted at frustration over the lapse in discipline. "When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate, it was very clear," Arteta stated. The incident serves as a harsh learning curve for the highly-rated teenager. First-team opportunities are precious for academy prospects, and a momentary loss of composure has now derailed his immediate integration into the senior setup. Premier League absence looms Dowman is now ruled out of Arsenal’s upcoming domestic schedule, missing pivotal Premier League fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City, and Newcastle. Over ten starts (36.2 innings), May put up a 5.65 ERA and 1.42 WHIP. Still, manager Pat Murphy turned to the veteran several times in the playoffs. After the Brewers clinched their World Series title on Wednesday, May announced that he and his wife are expecting their first child . May, once a highly touted pitcher in the Dodgers ‘ system, has had an up and down MLB career. During his first few years in the majors, he was known as a fireballer. The Dodgers eventually traded the hurler to the Red Sox on July 31st, 2025. After a brief stint in Boston, May signed a one-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals last offseason. (Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UW and Nebraska face off in Lincoln this weekend for the first time as conference foes. The long and storied history between the two teams stretches exactly 101 years and two weeks to the day between the very first match up in 1925 and this Saturday’s game. That shared history primarily revolves around the four games played during the 1990s when both programs were at their peak. The 1991 game featured a furious second half comeback in Lincoln that built the momentum towards UW’s eventual national championship. The Cornhuskers’ return trip to Seattle in 1992 set the stage for the loudest recorded home crowd in college football history. Five years later, Nebraska returned to Montlake to get their revenge for the previous two games while on their way to their own national championship in 1997 in Tom Osborne’s final season. For these two programs, the current stakes of this weekend’s game are much lower, although not entirely without significance. Both Washington and Nebraska enter Saturday night’s matchup at a crossroads in their seasons. Nebraska sits at 5-2 overall and 2-2 in Big Ten play, but the Cornhuskers are coming off consecutive close losses to Indiana and Oregon. Despite those defeats, Matt Rhule’s team has established itself as one of the league’s most physical and statistically dominant defenses, keeping every game within reach through disciplined play, strong linebacker action, and excellent situational defense. Washington, meanwhile, is 4-3 overall and 1-3 in conference play. The Huskies snapped a three-game losing streak with a 38-26 victory over Purdue before their bye week and arrive in Lincoln needing momentum to salvage their Big Ten campaign. Jedd Fisch’s offense remains heavily dependent on its passing attack, ranking among the conference’s better aerial units, but questions at quarterback and a struggling rushing offense persist. Defensive Overview Over Matt Rhule’s four years at Nebraska, the Cornhuskers have embraced a physical and gritty, defensive-oriented identity as a program. item.description: Braves make no-brainer $24M Ronald Acuna Jr., Ozzie Albies decision to keep core intact for 2027 originally appeared on The Sporting News . The Atlanta Braves have another important offseason ahead of them and need to navigate it correctly, as there are still several areas where the team needs to improve. Not only will they have free agency decisions to make, but they will also need to determine which players to bring back before allowing others to test the market. Atlanta didn't end the season the way it wanted to, losing two consecutive home games to the Los Angeles Dodgers . One of the players who had the toughest time was Ronald Acuña Jr., who was booed by fans. Despite all of that, he made it clear that he wanted to stay in Atlanta. “I want to stay here, that hasn't changed. But I can't control that,” Acuña told the media. The futures of Ozzie Albies and Acuña are in the Braves' hands, as the team recently had to make decisions on both players. Each had a club option for 2027, and Sports Illustrated's Harrison Smajovits believed exercising them should be an easy decision for Atlanta. “It's now officially the offseason, and the Atlanta Braves can get to work, for at least the next month, getting their roster assembled for the 2027 season. Two moves to ensure continuity can be made pretty quickly. They have two club options to exercise this offseason: one for Ozzie Albies and the other for Ronald Acuña Jr. Albies would be due just $7 million. Acuña would get a $17 million check. Both numbers are according to Spotrac. All the Braves have to do is make the obvious decision on both. Yes, these are two very easy calls to make,” Smajovits wrote. The Braves made the easy decision Thursday night, exercising the club options for both Acuña and Albies. “The Braves today exercised options for OF Ronald Acuña Jr. and INF Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season,” the Braves posted. This was a no-brainer for Atlanta, as both decisions were relatively inexpensive and made sense for the organization. Next season, however, could be when the Braves have to decide whether to offer Albies a new contract or move on. The duo consists of two of the Braves' longest-tenured players and two of the few remaining members of the World Series team. At the very least, Atlanta will have both players back for the 2027 season. item.description: Manchester United v AFC Bournemouth - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Michael Carrick has insisted he is "not surprised" to remain in the Manchester United dugout despite the club enduring their most disastrous start to a league season in four decades. The former England international saw his position come under intense scrutiny this week following a dismal 3-0 home defeat at the hands of Bournemouth. Surviving the Old Trafford cull Carrick looked certain to face the axe following Sunday's humiliating loss against the Cherries . That result extended an abysmal winless streak to eight matches in all competition, cementing the club's worst start to a league campaign in 40 years. However, crisis talks were held on Monday between the 45-year-old and the United hierarchy. Despite widespread anticipation of a managerial change, the boardroom ultimately opted to keep him at the helm . This backing comes just months after Carrick penned a new permanent two-year deal in the summer. He had earned the permanent role by securing Champions League football, having originally taken over as a short-term successor to Ruben Amorim in January. Tuning out the noise When pressed on his survival, the former midfielder maintained a defiant stance. He insisted his sole focus remains on rectifying the current crisis on the pitch rather than fearing for his job. "No, I am here to do my job and do my job for the team," Carrick told reporters. "I'm desperate to make us better and improve things, so I'm not surprised, no. I said after the [Bournemouth] game that I didn't expect anything. I was dealing with the performance and the result." Addressing the hostile atmosphere during the Bournemouth defeat, he added: "There was no hiding that the dynamics in the stadium were a bit different from normal. My mind was going through that and digesting that as I mentioned to [the media] after the game. It was purely that my mind was [thinking] 'what do we need to do to improve things?'" He acknowledged the immense pressure of the Old Trafford hot seat but dismissed the impact of external speculation. "I don't need any assurances from anyone," he declared. item.title: ‘Needs To Have a Backbone,’ ‘Be a Normal Human’ — Sophie Cunningham Lays Out Demands for Next WNBA Commissioner, Draws Adam Silver Comparison
item.description: 'Needs To Have a Backbone,' 'Be a Normal Human' -- Sophie Cunningham Lays Out Demands for Next WNBA Commissioner, Draws Adam Silver Comparison With Cathy Engelbert set to leave her position as WNBA commissioner at the end of 2026, the search for her successor is an important moment for the league. Sophie Cunningham has a clear idea of what the next leader should bring to the role, and she believes the NBA’s Adam Silver offers a good example. Sophie Cunningham Wants Next WNBA Commissioner to Follow Adam Silver’s Approach to Player Relations Speaking on This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von, Cunningham praised Silver for the relationship he has built with NBA players. She believes the WNBA needs someone similar. “I think Adam Silver does a phenomenal job of having a relationship with his NBA players,” Cunningham said . “And so I just think that’s what we need on the W side.” The Indiana Fever guard then made it clear that the next commissioner must be confident enough to stand by their decisions, explaining: “We need someone to come in here who has a backbone, who’s going to stick to what they do, and hold the standard.” The 30-year-old added that the WNBA needs a common goal that can bring players, owners and other stakeholders together. For her, however, leadership is not just about making major decisions. She also wants the next commissioner to have basic communication skills and show respect to the people working in the league. Cunningham used a hypothetical example of a commissioner walking into a room without even greeting a player to explain her point. “Like, we’re in the room. Like, say hi, be human, be nice,” she said. “I think that’s all we’re really asking for is a little bit of respect and just be a normal human. We’re all trying to work for the same goal. We all want to make the WNBA the best it can be.” SEE ALSO: ‘I’m Proud to Be an American Citizen’ — Sophie Cunningham Makes Her Stance Clear Amid WNBA Finals Anthem Controversy She also stressed that the next leader must maintain open communication and support both players and owners, even when their interests do not always match. Cunningham acknowledged that players will not get everything they ask for, but believes having an open line of communication and mutual respect is essential. These comments build on Cunningham’s earlier thoughts about the commissioner search. She had previously spoken about the importance of player relations and discussed the role with Silver after he reached out to her. Cunningham’s comments come as Engelbert prepares to step down after more than seven years in charge. During her tenure, the WNBA experienced significant growth. In 2024, the league recorded 2.35 million regular-season attendees, a 48% increase from the previous year, while attracting more than 54 million unique viewers across its national television partners. The league has also expanded from 12 teams, with plans to reach 18 by 2030. MORE: ‘She Can’t Believe He Chose Philly,’ ‘2 GOATS’ – Fans React
